name: Typical colour vision
who: The baseline most map designs are checked against.

name: Deuteranopia
who: Red–green colour vision deficiency, the most common type. Around 8% of men have some red–green deficiency; most are milder than this simulation.

name: Protanopia
who: Red–green deficiency in which reds also look darker. Red symbols lose contrast as well as hue.

name: Tritanopia
who: Blue–yellow deficiency. Rare from birth, but age-related losses run along this same axis, so it's a useful stand-in for many older map readers.

name: Greyscale print
who: Photocopies, mono laser prints, SAR briefing handouts and e-ink GPS screens. Only lightness survives.

name: Red headtorch
who: Reading a paper map at night with a red light to keep night vision. Red ink reflects like blank paper and disappears.
